items.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007
items.q: My first well of course Mary Lou Williams and all those boogie woogie guys that — my dad got me these albums ... So that really influenced me.

ctx.x: Were you a word person when you listened to the music? Did you really pay attention to the words?

No I really didn’t. And I think part of that comes from my jazz roots which are really not vocal roots. My father, my family had all kinds of music. No blues in our — uh that came later with me. But I remember we had like Mary Lou Williams — 78s — that was what was records when I was a kid. And you could hear her music in my music and you can hear her music in my brother’s playing. My brother is a jazz pianist, doesn’t play any blues, and I’m a blues pianist, don’t play any jazz, and you can hear Mary Lou…
Did Mary Lou Williams also — I don’t want to read anything into that — but did she represent something to you being a woman professional musician?
